_label: baseline — PROVISIONAL TESTING VALUES. Simulation assumptions, NOT design locks.
name: baseline

career._label: PROD-013 (designer 2026-11-11): a FIXED career that ends by years OR by number of productions (the player picks at game start; default 20 years), then a recap and 'keep playing?'. Continuing never changes the locked legacy score. Legacy score = Prestige + 500 per Hall of Fame title + 1 point per $2,500 cash *(test)*; cash weighted so money-led (TV, streaming) and Prestige-led (awards) careers land within ~25% of each other at 20 years. Legacy overlay: off (no end).

legacyScore._hallOfFameFormatWeightLabel: Format balance 2026-11-12 (Claude's call): a 12-week limited series in the Hall of Fame counts half a title (a 30-week movie or a whole TV show counts 1), so short series can't stack legacy. TEST VALUE.

start._cashLabel: Producers default (test): $160K covers the first studio-funded 30-week movie ($60K base + ~$72K payroll for 2 staff + a cheap Star). Legacy overlay: $40K.

genreFamilyWeights._label: Designer 2026-11-11: Star fit leans on TWO families per genre, so a Funny+Romantic Star beats a Funny+Scary Star in a RomCom at equal Funny. Fit = weighted skill; per-film practice is split the same way. The first family listed is the genre's main family (world.genres). Secondary pairings and weights are CLAUDE'S PICKS for review *(test)*. legacy-advance.json sets null (one family per genre).

compatibility._label: Combo fit. ONE shared grade per EXACT genre+theme pair, applied identically to Audience and Critic scores (PROD-062). Audience/Critic differences come only from craft weights (audienceWeights 35% Filming + 35% Editing vs criticWeights 35% Plot + 35% Writing). mode editorial = DEFAULT since 2026-11-11 (designer approved the matrix). mode random = legacy regression only: two independent weighted grades from the world stream (every earlier gate). mode editorial = the designer-editable matrix below, optionally shifted by a bounded per-pair variation from a stable hash of (seed, pair), never a shared RNG stream. The random draws are still consumed in editorial mode so every other world/talent draw is unchanged. Grades are EDITORIAL PROPOSALS for designer review; 'contestable' pairs carry the pick and the reason.

variation._label: bounded world-to-world variation: each pair's single grade shifts one step with this chance (direction 50/50, clamped A..F).

contestable.Action|Dinosaurs: B (draft A/C). Huge crowd concept, but usually dumb fun; B keeps it a strong pick without being a no-brainer A.
contestable.Comedy|Sports: A (draft A/B). Sports comedy is a proven sweet spot (underdog team + slapstick); deserves top fit.
contestable.Comedy|Zombies: B (draft B/B). Zombie comedy works (spoof energy) but is a niche; B, not A.
contestable.Horror|Spies: D (draft D/F). Strange mix, not nonsense; keep F for pairings that fight each other outright.
contestable.Horror|Pirates: C (draft C/D). Cursed-ship / ghost-crew horror is a real subgenre; middling, not bad.
contestable.Thriller|Time Travel: A (draft B/A). Loops, paradoxes and countdowns are thriller fuel; one of the best thriller fits.
contestable.Romance|Zombies: D (draft D/F). Can work as a rare oddball love story; poor, not impossible.
contestable.Romance|Robots: C (draft D/C). Lonely-human/AI love stories land often enough; average fit.
contestable.Drama|Zombies: C (draft D/C). Survival drama with zombies as backdrop is a proven prestige-TV shape; average fit.
contestable.SciFi|Dinosaurs: B (draft B/C). De-extinction / lost-world sci-fi is the genre's natural home for dinosaurs.
contestable.RomCom|Zombies: D (draft D/F). Comedy softens the gore a little; still poor.
contestable.RomCom|Spies: C (draft B/D). Married-spies action romcom is popular but rarely good; split the difference.
contestable.Thriller|Dinosaurs: B (draft D). Designer 2026-11-11: dinosaurs on the loose is a natural thriller.
contestable.Action|Mythology: A (draft B). Designer 2026-11-11 asked why Mythology was never good: gods-and-heroes epics are a top action fit.
contestable.Romance|Vampires: A (draft B/D, first pick B). Designer 2026-11-11: Romance had no A; brooding immortal romance is its biggest crowd fit.
contestable.RomCom|Time Travel: A (draft B/C). Designer 2026-11-11: RomCom had no A; the time-loop / do-over romcom is a proven sweet spot.

compatibility._matrixNote: Collapse rule for the old two-grade draft: crowd genres (Action, Comedy, Horror, Romance, SciFi, RomCom) keep the draft AUDIENCE grade, prestige genres (Drama, Thriller) keep the draft CRITIC grade; contestable pairs use the pick above.

cult._label: Gate 4Q EXPERIMENT, default OFF. Rare audience-only reception exception at release ('Unexpected cult appeal'). Eligible only when: the pair's audience grade is in eligibleAudienceGrades, the studio has never released this exact pair before (novelty), and audience-side craft (mean Filming+Editing quality) >= minAudienceCraft. chance = baseChance + trend bonus; drawn from the lazy 'reception' stream. Success replaces the AUDIENCE grade used in the normal score formula (lift = +liftSteps; breakout = breakoutGrade) for THIS title only; critics, meters, Star, money untouched (money follows the normal audience model). The combo book keeps the true baseline grade.

world._grossPerViewerLabel: Movie ticket price. Designer 2026-11-11: movies take 30 weeks now, so tickets went $2 → $4 *(test)* to keep a movie's money per production-week in line with TV and limited series (reports/formats/summary.md). Legacy overlay: $2.

approaches._label: PROD-220 (Claude's call, designer delegated 2026-11-11): one planning choice instead of GDS's sliders. Crowd-pleaser leans crew effort to Filming + Editing (the Audience craft weights), Awards bait to Plot + Writing (the Critic weights); total effort unchanged. Multipliers *(test)*. Legacy overlay: off.
approaches._scoreShiftLabel: Added after the first check: effort alone barely moved veteran films (meters saturate) and Awards bait had no payoff. A flat tilt after the meter curve makes the choice visible all career *(test)*.
approaches._payoffLabel: Each approach must win in its own currency (otherwise Balanced dominates): Crowd-pleaser = more money, less Prestige; Awards bait = more Prestige, less money *(test)*.

production._formatTimeLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: production time fastest → slowest is limited series (12 wks), TV season (8 + 1.2/episode: 14/20/26/32 wks for 5/10/15/20), movie (30 wks). Money per production-week is evened out via ticket / per-episode prices (reports/formats/summary.md). TEST VALUES. Legacy overlay restores 16 / 18 / 6 + 2.
production._formatExperienceLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: experience per release by format (Star level progress + per-film practice growth, studio genre XP). A 30-week movie teaches 2x a short series. Limited series 1 -> 0.8 on 2026-11-12 (format balance, Claude's call: it also weights review Prestige, and 2.5 limited series fit in one movie's time). Legacy overlay: null (1 for everything).

staffGrowth._payLabel: Designer 2026-11-11, TEST VALUES: payroll + upkeep are paid MONTHLY (accrued weekly, paid every payrollPeriodWeeks; same total). Raises: wage = base x (1 + raisePerLevel x staff level), capped at +maxRaise; a staff level comes every 200 XP (~20 working weeks), so ~+40% by year 5 and ~+80% by year 10. Hires ask more when skilled (hireWage x average stat / 25). Engineers keep a fixed wage. Legacy overlay: weekly, no raises, flat hire wage.

studioGenre._qualityBonusLabel: PROD-026 (Claude's call, designer delegated 2026-11-11): 3% → 5% per genre level *(test)*, so specialising is felt (~+0.4 rookie / ~+0.17 veteran at level 5, docs/plans/star-xp-worth.md). Legacy overlay: 3%.
studioGenre._awardTiming: WORKING ASSUMPTION: genre XP awarded on production completion

scoring._starScoreBonusLabel: PROD-051 option B (designer 2026-11-11), TEST VALUES: a flat Star bonus AFTER the meter curve, sized by skill fit (never Fame): Audience += audience x fit/100, Critic += critic x fit/100. Fit 80 = +0.40 / +0.16 = about +0.3 average, the same all career. The Star's Filming points (production.starFilmingWeight) still apply on top. taperFrom (8 by default, designer 2026-11-11; null = off) fades the bonus to 0 between that score and 10, to protect the 9.0 Hall of Fame line (reports/star-xp/bonus-check.md). criticStoryGate: critics credit the Star only as far as the story holds up: the critic part scales from 0 at a Plot+Writing average of zeroAt to full at fullAt (default 50 → 75; story meters: early-film median ~62, career median ~74). null = off. Legacy overlay sets 0.

pool._label: Stars rework (PROD-213…218). Persistent talent pool generated ONCE at game creation from the seed (own 'pool' RNG stream, so no other draw moves), a yearly debut class, offscreen careers + retirement, years active (Fame correlates with career length), per-Star hidden growth weights rolled from internal templates, a catalog that unlocks with the first studio upgrade, an 'original lead' card on sequels/new seasons, and a useful free fallback Star. ALL NUMBERS ARE TEST VALUES. legacy-advance.json turns the whole block off (legacy byte-identical).
pool._fameLabel: Fame inside the tier band = lo + (hi - lo) x (fameByYears x yearsPosition + (1 - fameByYears) x random): more years active -> generally more Fame.

offscreen._label: Once a year every non-retired Star not cast in your current production ages one year, may retire, then may rise (Fame up, maybe a level) or fade (Fame down). 'young' = fewer than youngYears years active. Tuned so the big-name tier holds ~30 active Stars over 10 years (reports/stars/summary.md).

growth._label: Per-Star hidden growth weights: a template (internal only, never shown) + per-family jitter, normalised. Level-up points go by these weights; per-film practice still adds growthPerProject to the worked family. levelUpPoints + 2 films x practice = budgetPerLevel, so the budget stays the limit.

catalog._label: Unlocks with the first studio upgrade (staff-capacity ladder). If the config has no ladder, it unlocks at unlockPrestigeWithoutLadder Prestige instead (the first ladder step's Prestige in gate3.json). Flags up to perfectFitTop catalog Stars with family skill >= perfectFitMin as 'perfect for this role'.

fallback._label: Free fallback Star (PROD-218, audit M1 Claude's call 2026-11-12): focusSkill in EVERY family the production's genre leans on, otherSkill elsewhere, so the blended fit is ~45 (an average paid newcomer, measured in reports/stars) in every genre and the total (45 + 45 + 3 x 3 = 99) stays inside the level-0 budget of 100 *(test)*.

audience._movieDudLabel: Producers dud fix (PROD-092/208), TEST VALUES: MOVIE-only word-of-mouth pivot (diffusion legs only); null = use qualityPivot. TV/limited series keep the global pivot (PROD-209). Legacy overlay sets null.
audience._qualityPivotLabel: Gate 4 SENSITIVITY knob: score where in-run buzz / word of mouth / episode retention turn from negative to positive (weekly diffusion + episodic models only). 5 = every earlier gate.
audience._fanDecayExactLabel: Audit 2026-11-12: true = weekly fan decay keeps an unrounded count (ip.fansExact), so small fan bases still fade (260 fans no longer stick at 260 forever). legacy-advance.json sets false (old weekly rounding).

diffusion._label: WORKING ASSUMPTION (Gate 2.5 candidate): finite awareness diffusion. Used only when legsModel = 'diffusion' (the Producers default since 2026-11-10; legacy overlay = geometric). movieBadInterestDecay = MOVIE-only override of badInterestDecay (null = global). Designer 2026-11-11 'cliff dive': 1.0 → 3.0 *(test)*, so a mediocre movie keeps a fine opening but its audience falls off a cliff (week-2 drop ~93–97% for 4–6 scores vs ~32–44% for 6+), leaving it near break-even.

prestige._tvMilestonesLabel: TV achievements (designer 2026-11-11, PROD-140), TEST VALUES. Earned by quality across seasons, never by episodes or airtime (PROD-135). Kept apart from 'milestones' so overlays that replace the main list keep them. Acclaimed season: a season averaging 8.5+ (each such season). Hit show: Season 3+ with a show average of 8+ (once per show). Long-runner: Season 5+ with every season 7+ (once per show). Amounts doubled 2026-11-12 (format balance, Claude's call): 400/600/800, so TV earns about the same Prestige per production-week as movies (reports/format-balance/summary.md); first sized 200/300/400. Legacy overlay sets [].
prestige._repeatScopeNote: WORKING ASSUMPTION (Open in v9.61): each milestone pays once per IP. Options: perRelease | perIP | career

research._themePurchaseLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: no buying unlocks for now. themePurchase false removes the $25K theme research option; themes come from staff pitches and trend inspiration (themeUnlocks). Legacy overlay sets true.

themeUnlocks._label: Designer 2026-11-11: free second route for themes. When a LOCKED theme's trend turns Hot, your team may get inspired and unlock it (chance per Hot wave *(test)*, a stable hash of seed + theme + week, never a shared RNG stream). Tuned so themes open at roughly the old pitch+purchase pace. Legacy overlay sets false.

genreUnlocks._label: PROD-091 (designer 2026-11-11). Genres open through the CREW, not money: when any staff member reaches a stat threshold, the matching genre opens (Game Dev Story-style staff growth). RomCom is a combo unlock (release at least one of each listed genre). Thresholds ease over time (easing) so nobody is stuck; nothing is ever handed out. No paid genre research (designer rejected it). Checked weekly, no RNG. THRESHOLDS ARE TEST VALUES. legacy-advance.json turns it off.
genreUnlocks._easingLabel: Designer 2026-11-11 (replaces the year-6 free unlock): from fromYear on, every skill threshold drops perYear points per full year, never below floor, so a struggling crew still opens genres itself (SciFi: Editing 60, 55 in year 5, 50 in year 6, ...).

debug._note: TEST-ONLY regression injection: none | advanceAsRevenue | fameIntoScore. Must be 'none' for real runs.

staffCapacity._label: Studio-wide max employees (PROD-020, LOCKED ladder 4 -> 6 -> 8); NOT a per-project crew cap. Default since 2026-11-12 (audit H3): upgrade 1 = $250K + 200 Prestige, upgrade 2 = $750K + 1,000 Prestige *(test costs)*. The first upgrade also unlocks the Star catalog (PROD-216). legacy-advance.json restores the historical uncapped behaviour ([999]).

agents._runwayStarReserveLabel: Harness agents only (2026-11-11): the runway rule also reserves a typical mid-tier Star fee before starting a movie. Legacy overlay: false.
agents._label: Agent-only heuristics (not game rules). legacyHeuristicStaffCaps reproduces pre-Gate-2.5 strategy hiring cutoffs (balanced 4, quality-first 5, others never hire). tvOrderPreference (Gate 3): Gate 3 agents order the largest allowed TV season up to this size ("max" or a number). useFiring / economicRenewal (Gate 3 follow-up, Gate 3 policies only): dismiss the weakest employee to make room for the Software Engineer or when cash < fireDebtThreshold; renew a show only while its last finished season netted >= renewMinNetPerWeek per production week (replaces the old fixed policy season limits). Both false = the original Gate 3 policies. Default since 2026-11-12 (audit M3): the default agents play the default game (no legacy hiring cutoffs, firing on, money-based renewal; the same values gate3/gate4 always used); legacy-advance.json pins the old ones.

studioSize._label: PROD-226 (designer 2026-11-12): "we're a bigger company now, the expectations are higher". Toughness added to BOTH audience and critic reviews after the 1st / 2nd studio upgrade (same scale method as critic generations: x(1 - t)). Tuned so each upgrade is still a net gain but the Hall of Fame stays rare. legacy-advance.json disables it. TEST VALUES.

expectations._label: EXPERIMENTAL (Gate 2.6). HARNESS PROXY for critic generations (named critics retiring, replaced by a tougher generation) and gentler audience-era expectations. Deterministic, calendar-based, applied after combo/weakness/fatigue/saturation and before the 0-10 clamp, at release time only (published scores never change). Disabled = previous behavior exactly. All numbers are TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

critics._adaptLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: each new critic generation makes things a little harder on arrival, then the studio adapts. A new generation arrives every generationYears (announced 26 weeks ahead) and cuts critic scores by toughnessPerGeneration; only permanentShare of that stays, the rest fades over adaptYears. Measured (15-yr careers): Hall of Fame rate dips after each arrival (yr 5: ~10% vs ~19%), then recovers and keeps rising late (yr 8 ~19%, yr 13 ~21%). TEST VALUES. Legacy overlay: off, and adaptYears null (permanent steps).

formats._label: Gate 3. LOCKED direction: movies + limited series first, TV via a studio upgrade (money + Prestige), streaming later. All false = the Gate 2.6 movie-only kernel, byte-identical.
formats._defaultLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: limited series and TV ship ON in the Producers default (TV still unlocks via the studio upgrade: Prestige + cash). Streaming ON since 2026-11-11 after the payback review (reports/streaming/summary.md). legacy-advance.json restores all false.

limitedSeries._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS. Self-contained, NON-renewable series: fixed episode package, weekly airing + short tail.
limitedSeries._grossPerEpisodeViewerLabel: Designer 2026-11-11: limited series take 12 weeks now; 0.57 → 0.40 *(test)* keeps them from out-earning everything per week. Legacy overlay: 0.57.

tv._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS for renewable TV (one IP, separately produced seasons). LOCKED: renewal by season average (4.0 renewable, 9.0 HoF), episode caps by studio Prestige (not show history), genre locked, twist changes theme, hiatus affects anticipation only, announcement = show-specific fading hype.
tv._grossPerEpisodeViewerLabel: Designer 2026-11-11 (PROD-209): a healthy TV season should pay about like a movie per week of production. 0.32 → 0.42 *(test)*, then 0.46 after the 2026-11-11 production-time change (TV ~$15K per production-week vs movies ~$16K, limited series ~$18K; reports/formats/summary.md). Legacy overlay keeps 0.32.

TV pay per episode-viewer *(test)*: 0.32 -> 0.42 (PROD-209) -> 0.46 (PROD-221 price rebalance) -> 0.36 (format balance 2026-11-12, Claude's call: with money-based renewal TV earned ~1.7x a movie per production-week; now ~1.15x, with TV achievements doubled for Prestige).

showHealth._label: Designer 2026-11-11 (PROD-139): bad seasons drive viewers away. Each prior season multiplies the show's returning audience (its reach cap) by 1 + slope x (season avg - pivot)/5, kept between floor and 1 (a great season can win viewers back up to full, never above). Pivot 7.5, slope 1.0: a 6.5 season keeps 80% of the audience, 7.0 keeps 90%, 7.5+ keeps everyone; two 6.5 seasons → 0.64. TEST VALUES. Legacy overlay turns it off.

viewerFatigue._label: EXPERIMENT (Gate 3 follow-up), default OFF. Returning-viewer / season-opening interest fatigue: multiplies ONLY the returning-audience opening inputs (IP fans + announcement anticipation; optionally the premiere share). Never touches Audience/Critic scores, ratings or sales directly. Separate from review fatigue (tv.fatigue), IP fans and hiatus. Offset by: previous-season quality (qualitySlow), a good twist (goodTwistReset units), and every additive opening input it does not touch (marketing, Star Fame, trends, studio buzz) plus in-run critic buzz / word of mouth. basis: seasons = seasons aired; episodes = episodes aired / episodesPerStep. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

contract._label: OPEN designer decision. A = every season is a new pitch (fixed offers). B = continuing partner: same distributor + royalty; per-season advance = baseCost x clamp(baseCover + roiWeight x (lastRoi-1), minCover, maxCover) x trust factor.

streaming._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS for the studio streaming service (one aggregate subscriber business; no per-title payouts).
streaming._reviewLabel: Designer 2026-11-11 review: after movies went to 30 weeks / $4 tickets, a platform never paid back (−$1.5M to −$8.8M by year 20). Subscription $0.50 → $0.75/sub/week *(test)*. Then (same day) the unlock moved later so streaming is the LATE-game milestone (designer: year ~6.6 felt early): 3,000 Prestige + 20 catalog titles *(test)*. Mixed studios launch ~year 9, break even ~year 12, +$3.3M by year 15, +$8.1M by year 20. Legacy overlay: $0.50, 2,500 Prestige, 8 titles.

staffing._label: Gate 3 follow-up. LOCKED: employees can be fired to free a capacity slot (4/6/8 unchanged; the Software Engineer uses a normal slot). Harness UX ASSUMPTIONS: dismissal only between productions; the engineer cannot be dismissed while building; minStaff and fireCost are OPEN (smallest rule protecting the 'production always progresses' invariant).

breakthrough._label: EXPERIMENT (Gate 3 follow-up), default OFF. Rare seeded creative breakthrough DURING production: one draw from the dedicated 'events' RNG stream when a production first enters each listed stage; on success, bonus meter points = bonusShare x that meter's half-point (meterHalfPointPerWeek x duration x era bar), so the effect saturates on already-strong meters and flows to scores only through the normal meter -> score formula. Never edits a result. At most maxPerProduction per production. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

economy._label: DEFAULT = late_distribution (PROD-100, Producers economy). mode legacy_advance = REGRESSION ONLY, every earlier gate byte-identical (distributor advances at the pitch, lifeline, surplus); select it with config/legacy-advance.json / legacyConfig(). mode late_distribution: the studio funds base cost, Star and payroll itself; at 80% 2-3 distributors bid ADVERTISING spend + reach for a revenue share (ad money is spent by the distributor, never studio cash); self-distribution fallback; no lifeline. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

overdraft._label: PROD-125 (Claude's call, designer delegated 2026-11-11): never game over. In the red you can't start productions or buy extras, and the debt costs monthlyRate interest each month *(test)*. Legacy overlay: 0.

lateDistribution._label: Candidate bid formula. appeal = 1 + previewWeight x (preview - previewCenter)/previewSpan + trend + fans + Star Fame + known combo (comboBook only) + last-season delta, clamped. Preview = visible meter quality so far, projected to completion (never final scores or hidden combo grades). adSpend = adBase x format factor x appeal x favored x trust factor x jitter; share = shareBase x (1.15 - 0.15 x appeal) x (1.1 - 0.04 x trust). A distributor only bids when appeal >= its minAppeal.

studioClout._label: PROD-227 (designer 2026-11-12): distributors compete harder for bigger studios. After the 1st / 2nd studio upgrade, every bid's ad budget is multiplied by adMultByUpgrades and the distributor's cut by shareMultByUpgrades, so a bigger studio earns back its bigger payroll. legacy-advance.json disables it. TEST VALUES.

contracts._label: Gate 4 EXPERIMENT: work-for-hire. Zero cost to accept; the client reimburses the studio's payroll + upkeep each contract week (ledger contract_labor) and pays a fixed visible completion fee (contract_fee). Staff gain XP/stats in the contract's meters. Zero Prestige, no IP, fans, release, HoF or catalog entry. One job at a time (uses the production slot). Fees are TEST ASSUMPTIONS. DEFAULT ON with the Producers economy (PROD-118); legacy-advance.json turns it off.
